channel.title: Rudra Techie: The Notebook
channel.description: AI, benchmarks, and building useful things.

item.title: Coding Agent Benchmarks Miss the Hard Part
item.description: Passing coding tasks is not the same as safely shipping changes. A practical look at what agent benchmarks reveal, what they leave out, and how to test a coding agent yourself.

item.title: RAG vs Long Context: Choose by Failure Mode
item.description: A clear engineering guide to retrieval-augmented generation and long context windows, with a decision framework based on freshness, corpus size, citations, and failure cost.

item.title: Write Technical Posts Without AI Slop
item.description: A practical workflow for writing original technical content that uses AI without losing your examples, judgement, evidence, or natural voice.

item.title: The Real Cost of AI Work
item.description: Measure AI project cost in retries, review, latency, maintenance and errors. A practical worksheet to decide whether a feature is earning its complexity.

item.title: LinkedIn AI Slop Is Making Us Worse at Thinking
item.description: Why synthetic polish spreads on LinkedIn, how it changes what we reward, and a practical way to make AI-assisted writing sound like you again.

item.title: An AI Benchmark Score Is Not a Verdict
item.description: How to read AI benchmarks without being fooled by a leaderboard. Learn to inspect task design, scoring, baselines, contamination, variance, and the gap between a score and your job.

item.title: Benchmark Contamination: When Tests Leak
item.description: What training data leakage means for AI benchmark scores, what contamination can and cannot prove, and how to evaluate models on genuinely fresh work.

item.title: How to Start Learning AI: A Practical Path
item.description: A practical AI learning path from Python and machine learning basics to language models, evaluation and a first useful project, with a weekly study loop.

item.title: Build an AI Project That Solves a Real Problem
item.description: A step-by-step framework to choose a personal AI project, define its success measure, build a safe prototype and learn from the results.

item.title: How to Start a Startup: Test the Problem First
item.description: A practical first step for starting a startup: speak to potential users, test whether the problem happens often, measure current workarounds and avoid mistaking compliments for demand.

item.title: When to Automate a Workflow
item.description: Decide whether to automate a repeated task using frequency, stability, error cost and human judgement. Includes a practical automation scorecard and safe rollout approach.

item.title: Setting Up Claude Code with the BMAD Method
item.description: A practical setup for using Claude Code with the current BMAD-METHOD: install versioned workflows, give the agent a clear project brief, and keep agile planning proportional.

item.title: Context Engineering for Coding Agents
item.description: A practical guide to repository instructions, task context, source-of-truth documents, code discovery and verification for coding agents like Claude Code.

item.title: Build a Practical AI Evaluation Set
item.description: Create a trustworthy first evaluation set for an AI project: collect representative examples, write success criteria before comparing models, score failures and retain regression tests.

item.title: Tokens, Context and Transformers: An LLM Guide
item.description: A beginner-friendly explanation of tokens, context windows, transformer attention and next-token prediction, with examples that help debug real language-model applications.

item.title: How to Read an AI Research Paper
item.description: A structured reading workflow for AI research papers: identify the research question, inspect methods and baselines, read result tables carefully and find limitations before trusting the headline.

item.title: Ship an AI Feature With a Safe Fallback
item.description: A launch checklist for a small AI feature covering user confirmation, output validation, data handling, monitoring, fallback behaviour and regression tests.

item.title: DeepSeek Harness and Cordis, Explained
item.description: A technical look at DeepSeek Harness, Cordis, its plugin architecture, traceable sessions and runtime modes, plus what builders should examine before calling it the future of agents.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon Benchmarks: What the Scores Miss
item.description: Google reports strong Gemini 4 Argon results, but what do the benchmark suites measure, which gains transfer to real work, and what does a different model cost?

item.title: Phonon-2: Open Speech Recognition on Device
item.description: A close look at Phonon-2's compact weights, reported word error rate, Apple Neural Engine speed, licensing and the real evaluation questions for local transcription.

item.title: What AI-Generated Math Proofs Actually Verify
item.description: How to assess OpenAI's October 2026 mathematics results: what the Lean formalizations establish, what the human-written manuscripts still need, and why discovery is not the same as verification.

item.title: Why Word Error Rate Isn't Enough
item.description: Understand how WER works, which transcript errors matter in practice, and how to build a speech recognition evaluation using your actual microphones, accents and vocabulary.

item.title: Compare AI Models on Cost, Latency and Quality
item.description: A repeatable method for comparing AI models on your own tasks, controlling prompts and tools while tracking success, retries, latency and total operating cost.
